note: Every `expected` block is produced by the real Python resolver (macros.resolve) -- either `{ops, report}` or `{error}`, the latter being the exact sentence MacroError carried. Both are compared in full by chrome-extension/test/macro-parity.mjs, because a refusal is part of the contract: replay that raises has not touched the page.

cases.name: exact-match
cases.why: role and name both equal: the base 0.6 plus 0.4, which is the .0 the report has to print as 1.0 rather than 1

cases.name: near-role-family
cases.why: a macro recorded against a menuitem resolving against a button: 0.55 + 0.4. The family exists because the same control is announced differently by different markup

cases.name: a-role-outside-the-family-is-not-a-candidate
cases.why: a checkbox is not a button however it is labelled: score 0, so there is nothing to compare and the run stops before touching the page

expected.error: step 1 (click on button 'Check in') did not match anything above 0.7: best=none

cases.name: case-and-collapsed-space
cases.why: `_norm` lowercases and collapses runs of space, so a macro recorded off a label that was re-flowed still matches

cases.name: a-zero-width-no-break-space-is-not-a-space-to-python
cases.why: U+FEFF is whitespace to JavaScript's `\s` and not to Python's `str.split()`. Folding it would make two different labels equal and score 1.0 where Python scores 0.8 -- a replay confident about the wrong element

cases.name: a-next-line-character-is-a-space-to-python
cases.why: U+0085 is whitespace to Python and not to JavaScript's `\s`, so the port has to call it one: the two sides agree on 1.0 only if the class is spelled out

cases.name: substring-either-way
cases.why: either direction of containment earns 0.2: a shortened label on the page and a lengthened one both land

cases.name: token-overlap-carries-a-reordered-name
cases.why: same words, different order, neither containing the other: the token overlap is 1.0 and the score is 0.6 + 0.2

cases.name: token-overlap-below-half-is-not-a-match
cases.why: a third of the words in common is not the same control, so the score is 0 and the step refuses rather than picking the nearest thing

expected.error: step 1 (click on button 'daily check in') did not match anything above 0.7: best=none

cases.name: a-nameless-target-still-matches
cases.why: a macro step with no name falls back to the role alone: 0.6 + 0.1, which is exactly the threshold and therefore passes. `>=` and `>` are the difference between a usable macro and a broken one

cases.name: the-threshold-is-what-refuses-a-weak-match
cases.why: a nameless target in a near-role family: 0.55 + 0.1 = 0.65, under 0.7, so it refuses. This is the only reachable score the default threshold rejects, and it is why the threshold is worth having

expected.error: step 1 (click on menuitem '') did not match anything above 0.7: best=[{'ref': 'e1', 'name': 'Check in', 'role': 'button', 'score': 0.65}]

cases.name: the-refusal-lists-what-it-considered
cases.why: when nothing clears the threshold the error names the top five in page order, so a human can see whether the macro is wrong or the page is. Order comes from a stable sort over equal scores

expected.error: step 1 (click on menuitem '') did not match anything above 0.7: best=[{'ref': 'e1', 'name': 'First', 'role': 'button', 'score': 0.65}, {'ref': 'e2', 'name': 'Second', 'role': 'button', 'score': 0.65}, {'ref': 'e3', 'name': 'Third', 'role': 'button', 'score': 0.65}, {'ref': 'e4', 'name': 'Fourth', 'role': 'button', 'score': 0.65}, {'ref': 'e5', 'name': 'Fifth', 'role': 'button', 'score': 0.65}]

cases.name: context-breaks-a-tie
cases.why: two identically-named buttons on different rows: context is worth 0.15, which clears the 0.06 margin, so the macro recorded on the right row wins instead of refusing

cases.name: a-tie-without-context-refuses
cases.why: the same two buttons with a macro that has no context: a perfect match on both sides is the silent misclick this design exists to prevent, so it raises instead of picking the first

expected.error: step 1 is ambiguous between e1 'Book' and e2 'Book'. Add distinguishing context to the macro or run the step manually.

cases.name: a-tie-inside-the-margin-refuses
cases.why: 1.0 against 0.95 -- a button and a link with the same label, which is what a styled anchor next to a real button looks like. 0.05 apart is inside the 0.06 margin, so the best match being perfect does not save it

expected.error: step 1 is ambiguous between e1 'Submit' and e2 'Submit'. Add distinguishing context to the macro or run the step manually.

cases.name: a-tie-from-two-token-scores-refuses
cases.why: 0.733 against 0.7, both from the 0.2 * overlap term: the margin is compared after `round(score, 3)`, so the rounding is part of the decision and not cosmetic

expected.error: step 1 is ambiguous between e1 'streak daily' and e2 'daily check bonus'. Add distinguishing context to the macro or run the step manually.

cases.name: context-below-its-overlap-floor-is-ignored
cases.why: context only counts at 0.4 token overlap, so a context that shares one word out of four adds nothing and the tie stands

expected.error: step 1 is ambiguous between e1 'Book' and e2 'Book'. Add distinguishing context to the macro or run the step manually.

cases.name: context-at-its-overlap-floor-counts
cases.why: 0.4 is the floor for a context to count and it is reached exactly here -- two of five words in common, one above a context that shares too little. The comparison is inclusive, and inclusive is what makes the tie breakable at all

cases.name: the-threshold-can-be-lowered
cases.why: the same 0.65 that the default rejects resolves at 0.6. Replay decides how sure it has to be; the resolver only measures

cases.name: cjk-exact-match-is-fine
cases.why: an exact CJK label never reaches the token branch -- equality is checked first -- so the ordinary case on a Chinese site resolves at 1.0

cases.name: cjk-substring-still-works
cases.why: containment is string-level, not token-level, so a label that only grew a suffix still resolves

cases.name: cjk-reordered-name-cannot-be-matched
cases.why: the same four characters in a different order: neither contains the other, and the token branch returns 0 because a CJK label has no tokens at all. Any reworded Chinese label is invisible to this resolver -- a real limit, reproduced here on purpose so the port does not paper over it

expected.error: step 1 (click on button '签到领奖') did not match anything above 0.7: best=none

cases.name: cjk-context-cannot-break-a-tie
cases.why: two Chinese buttons with the same label and different context: the context bonus needs tokens on both sides, gets none, and the tie refuses. On a Chinese site every context in a macro is inert, so a repeated label is unresolvable however carefully it was recorded

expected.error: step 1 is ambiguous between e1 '签到' and e2 '签到'. Add distinguishing context to the macro or run the step manually.

cases.name: the-same-tie-in-english-resolves
cases.why: the control for the case above: identical markup, English labels, and the context bonus does its job. The difference between these two cases is the whole bug

cases.name: a-template-becomes-its-parameter
cases.why: the recorded DuckDuckGo macro, with the query filled in. One macro file, any search

cases.name: a-missing-parameter-is-left-alone
cases.why: no value supplied means the target keeps the literal `{{query}}` rather than becoming an empty search. A macro that silently sends nothing is worse than one that sends the wrong thing visibly

cases.name: parameters-are-stringified-the-way-python-does-it
cases.why: a number, a boolean, a dotted name and a placeholder padded with spaces: Python's `str()` gives `42`, `True` and the raw text, and a port that reaches for JavaScript's `String()` gets two of those wrong

cases.name: only-the-fields-the-macro-has-reach-the-op
cases.why: a `type` with no `submit` must not grow one, or a replay would press Enter on a form the recording never submitted

cases.name: every-op-field-survives-resolution
cases.why: one step per field the resolver carries: text, value, key, state, dir, amount, ms, paths. A field dropped here is a replay that types the wrong thing

cases.name: an-empty-string-is-still-a-field-the-macro-set
cases.why: clearing a field is an operation, not an omission: Python writes `text: ''` because the key is present, while a port that tests truthiness drops the step's whole point and leaves the old value in the box

cases.name: an-empty-path-list-is-not-a-path-list
cases.why: `[]` is falsy in Python and truthy in JavaScript. An upload step with no paths has nothing to attach, and the two languages only agree here if the length is checked -- `if (step.paths)` would hand the executor an empty list to open

cases.name: an-empty-scroll-direction-is-not-a-direction
cases.why: the same falsy-empty trap on `dir`: with no direction there is no amount either, so the executor supplies both. Writing `dir: ''` and a default 600 would turn a step the recording never really made into a full-screen scroll

cases.name: a-zero-millisecond-wait-is-not-a-wait
cases.why: the third falsy field, after `dir` and `paths`: `ms: 0` is skipped in Python because a wait of no time is not a wait, and the executor's own default is what applies. A port that tests presence schedules a zero-length timer the recording never had

cases.name: a-name-overlap-just-below-half-is-still-nothing
cases.why: 0.4 in common is under the 0.5 floor, so the element is not a candidate at all and the refusal says `best=none`. That floor is a decision about what counts as the same control, and moving it by a tenth turns this refusal into a 0.68 near-miss -- a different sentence in the report, which is how the fixtures notice

expected.error: step 1 (click on button 'daily check streak goal') did not match anything above 0.7: best=none

cases.name: an-explicit-zero-amount-is-not-the-default
cases.why: `amount: 0` is a real value and `600` is only the fallback for a missing key. Python's `dict.get(key, default)` tests presence, and `|| 600` in a port would silently turn a no-op scroll into a full screen

cases.name: a-scroll-without-a-direction-takes-both-defaults
cases.why: no `dir` means neither field is written at all -- the executor supplies them

cases.name: upload-paths-are-substituted-one-by-one
cases.why: a path list is the one field where the template runs per item rather than once over the whole value

cases.name: ops-without-a-target-pass-straight-through
cases.why: a key press and a wait have nothing to resolve against, so they reach the executor untouched. Not every step is about an element

cases.name: an-empty-target-is-treated-as-no-target
cases.why: `{}` is a falsy dict in Python and a truthy object in JavaScript. The distinction is invisible until a macro carries a bare empty target, at which point the two languages disagree about whether there is anything to match

cases.name: steps-without-an-op-are-skipped-without-renumbering
cases.why: a step that is not an operation is dropped, but the numbers the rest are reported under still come from the file, so a report line matches the macro a human opens

cases.name: a-recorded-failure-replays-predictably
cases.why: `tmp-1p3a-scratch.json`: twelve identical clicks recorded while the HOVER gap made the real target unreachable. Every step resolves to the same element at 1.0 and the replay would do exactly what the recording did. Predictable is not the same as correct, which is why replay ends in a `verify`

cases.name: the-fossil-after-the-gap-was-closed
cases.why: the same trigger once the menu it hides is in the table: the hover step is what reaches it, and this is the macro that should have been recorded

cases.name: a-live-page-and-the-menu-behind-its-trigger
cases.why: the path that matters: a hover step onto the trigger, then a click on the menu item that only exists afterwards. Both resolve at 1.0 against a payload the real observer produced, which is the whole premise of replaying this task
